records.description_en: A multi-channel temperature controller that reads multiple temperature sensor inputs and drives heater outputs for setpoint regulation, ramped temperature changes, and heater power control. It is commonly used for sample temperature monitoring and stabilization in laboratory experiments.

This is a two-axis motion controller for driving micro-positioning axes. It controls X and Y axes for relative stepping, continuous jogging, motion toward limits, and zero-position definition, with adjustable step amplitude and step delay. It is commonly used for optical alignment, precision micro-positioning, and dual-axis positioning tasks in laboratory setups.

A motion controller for Newport Agilis two-axis piezo stepper stages or micropositioners. It controls X and Y axes and supports relative motion, continuous jogging, limit seeking, and status monitoring, making it suitable for optical alignment, precision positioning, and micromanipulation experiments.

An AMI superconducting magnet used to generate and stably control magnetic fields in experiments, typically driven by a magnet power supply and configured through a current-to-field conversion relationship. It is commonly used in scenarios requiring stable external fields, including cryogenic physics, quantum-device experiments, and materials characterization.

A robotic manipulator with a gripper that can be controlled by end-effector pose, tool-center-point pose, or joint state, suitable for laboratory grasping, transfer, positioning, and automation experiments.

A multi-axis hardware controller for microscopy and automated experiments. It communicates over serial to control motorized stages/axes and can coordinate scanning, filter wheels, dichroic sliders, logic triggering, waveform output, and timing signals for cameras, lasers, and remote focus devices.

The Andor Neo is a scientific CMOS camera for low-noise, high-sensitivity 2D imaging in laboratories. It is commonly used for microscopy, optical measurements, and scientific image acquisition experiments that require adjustable exposure, sensor readout settings, and region-of-interest selection.

A scientific imaging camera for laboratory image acquisition, supporting exposure control, frame readout, ROI configuration, buffer management, sensor temperature handling, and shutter-related control for applications such as microscopy.

A cooled scientific CCD camera for low-light imaging, spectroscopy detection, and time-resolved acquisition in the laboratory. The device supports detector temperature control, shutter and trigger control, configurable readout speeds and gain, and acquisition of single-frame or continuous image data.

An Andor scientific camera is a laboratory imaging device used to acquire low-noise, high-sensitivity 2D image data. It is commonly used for microscopy, spectroscopy detection, and general scientific image acquisition in research experiments.

This is an image/array gathering plugin component used in an area detector acquisition pipeline. It typically sits downstream of another areaDetector plugin, receives NDArray data from a source plugin, and groups or gathers the data for later display, processing, or file output. It is commonly used in synchrotron, microscopy, and other 2D detector-based experimental workflows.

records.name_en: Ark Metrica Stepper Motor Linear Motion Controller
records.description_en: A stepper-motor-based linear motion controller for a linear actuator or positioning stage. It communicates over serial/VISA and supports device identification, speed and acceleration settings, homing, moving to a target position, position readback, and emergency stop for laboratory sample or probe positioning tasks.

This is a BACnet-compatible building automation field device or controller used to interface with HVAC equipment, environmental sensors, actuators, utility meters, and alarm points. It exposes device and object information on the network and allows properties of points to be read or written. In laboratories and research facilities, such devices are commonly used for room environmental monitoring, HVAC and ventilation coordination, energy data collection, and facility infrastructure integration.

A charge-coupled device detector used for optical measurements, converting incident light into digital spectral or imaging data. It is commonly integrated with spectrometers, monochromators, or Raman systems, and supports configuration of exposure, gain, readout speed, region of interest, triggering, and wavelength-related settings; some models provide EM gain.

An integrated temperature sensor inside the processor used to read the CPU thermal-zone temperature. In laboratory and computing setups, it is used for thermal management, over-temperature alarms, cooling evaluation, and temperature-rise monitoring during load testing.
A laboratory laser light source used for illumination and optical excitation in microscopy, fluorescence excitation, and other optical experiments.

A controllable laboratory laser source with switchable emission and adjustable output power, commonly used for microscopy, fluorescence excitation, and general optical experiments requiring stable illumination.

This is a compact laboratory laser source that provides controlled optical output power and supports modulation operating modes. It is commonly used for microscopy, fluorescence excitation, optical alignment, and other experiments or instruments that require stable laser illumination or excitation light.

A Cobolt laser is a compact laboratory laser source that provides stable continuous-wave laser output, commonly used for optical experiments, beam alignment, optical setups, and fluorescence-related measurements.

The Coherent OBIS is a compact laboratory laser source that provides stable laser output with controllable power and on/off operation. It is commonly used for microscopy, fluorescence excitation, optical alignment, and other experiments requiring a stable continuous light source.

This is a Coherent Sapphire series laser that provides stable continuous laser output. Such lasers are commonly used for microscopy, fluorescence excitation, optical alignment, and other laboratory applications requiring a stable light source, with support for laser on/off control and power adjustment.

This is a tunable ultrafast laser made by Coherent. It provides laser output over a selectable wavelength range and supports wavelength tuning, group-delay-dispersion compensation, shutter control, and alignment mode. Such systems are commonly used in multiphoton microscopy, ultrafast spectroscopy, nonlinear optics, and other experiments requiring a tunable short-pulse laser source.

records.name_en: CoolLED pE Series Microscope LED Illumination Controller
records.description_en: A multi-channel LED illumination controller and light source system for microscopes, commonly used in fluorescence imaging. It provides multiple independent wavelength channels (such as A to H) for exciting different fluorophores, with channel selection, on/off control, and TTL triggering.

A high-precision piezo positioning device for microscopy experiments. It can move a channel to a target position and report current position, travel limits, controller ready status, and channel-related information. It is typically used for fine focus or nanometer-scale motion control.

A hardware controller for piezo positioning channels. It can move a selected channel to a target position, read the current position, and query control readiness, channel object, channel phase, and position limits. It is commonly used for precision microscope focusing and nanoscale positioning.
The EIGER is a hybrid-pixel photon-counting X-ray area detector used to acquire diffraction or scattering images in synchrotron and laboratory X-ray experiments.

The EIGER is a pixelated X-ray area detector used to collect two-dimensional diffraction or scattering images in experiments, commonly in synchrotron, crystallography, and X-ray scattering applications.

This is a positioner controller used in EMC and antenna test systems to control motion, target position, travel limits, and vertical/horizontal polarization selection. It is commonly used in anechoic chambers or automated test setups to drive antenna masts, scanning mechanisms, or similar motion platforms for positioning and sweeps.

A non-physical software component for experiment automation that orchestrates EPICS step-scan workflows. It configures positioners, detectors, triggers, counters, and extra PVs, then executes point-by-point scans, acquires data, handles pause/abort logic, publishes per-point data, and writes scan output files.

A motorized laboratory motion axis controlled through an EPICS motor record, typically attached to a linear stage, rotation stage, or other electromechanical actuator. It is used for precision positioning, scanning, homing, and travel-limit management in beamlines, optical setups, and sample-handling systems.

A compact embedded camera module based on ESP32 that transmits image data over a serial connection and supports basic imaging parameter adjustment. It is suitable for low-cost live preview, simple image capture, setup observation, and experiment documentation in laboratory environments.

An embedded network camera module based on the ESP32, typically integrating an image sensor, Wi‑Fi connectivity, and an onboard illumination LED. It can deliver single images or video streams over the network and supports adjustment of gain, exposure, and frame size. It is suitable for low-cost remote observation, sample monitoring, simple machine vision, and imaging documentation in laboratory setups.

This is a 1-to-12 microfluidic distributor/selector valve used to route a single fluid line to multiple channels or sample paths. It is commonly used in microfluidics experiments, automated reagent delivery, sample switching, and multi-line fluid path management.

This device is a multi-channel pressure controller for microfluidic experiments, providing precise pneumatic actuation for chips, reservoirs, and fluidic circuits. It can read pressure on each channel and work with flow or pressure sensors for monitoring, calibration, and closed-loop PID control, making it suitable for stable low-flow delivery, droplet generation, and microfluidic flow regulation.

The Eurotherm 2408 is a panel-mounted temperature/process controller used to regulate heating systems in laboratories and industrial setups. It reads temperature sensor signals and provides closed-loop control of furnaces, heaters, or thermal processes through setpoint control, PID tuning, ramp rate settings, manual/automatic modes, and power output adjustment.

A multi-actuator control system built around Feetech bus-connected smart servos and their serial communication bus. It is commonly used in laboratory robotic platforms such as robot arms and grippers to read status such as position and send control commands such as target position.

The FireSting is a multi-channel optical oxygen meter designed to work with optical oxygen sensors. It performs optical oxygen measurements in liquid or gas samples and can apply temperature, pressure, and salinity compensation. It is commonly used in laboratories for dissolved oxygen, oxygen saturation, and related oxygen monitoring.

A PyroScience FireSting series optical oxygen meter for fiber-optic or probe-based oxygen sensors. It performs oxygen measurements, zero/air calibration, background correction, and reads temperature, pressure, humidity, and result registers for dissolved-oxygen or gas-phase oxygen experiments.

This is a three-axis motorized positioning stage driven by a GRBL motion controller, typically using stepper motors for X, Y, and Z travel with homing and position readback. In laboratories it is commonly used for microscope sample positioning, automated scanning, focus translation, and small-scale motion automation.

This is a GRBL-based 3-axis motorized motion stage, typically driven by an Arduino Uno and CNC shield to control X, Y, and Z stepper motors. It supports homing, limit switches, relative and absolute positioning, and simple laser intensity and LED control, making it useful for moving, positioning, and shaking sample plates, stages, or small laboratory automation mechanisms.

A serially controlled motion control board based on GRBL firmware, used to drive X/Y/Z stages, linear slides, or simple CNC/laser setups for positioning and motion. It supports homing, coordinate moves, speed and acceleration settings, and control of laser intensity or LED output, making it useful in laboratories for sample positioning, scan-path execution, and automated translation tasks.

A CNC motion control device running GRBL firmware, receiving G-code commands over a serial connection to drive multi-axis motion. It is commonly used in small CNC engravers, positioning stages, or laser processing systems, and in laboratories for sample positioning, automated scanning, trajectory motion, and simple machining control.

This device class comprises laboratory instruments that support the GSIOC serial communication protocol, typically over an RS-422/485 bus. They can be addressed and controlled by unit ID on a shared serial bus and are commonly used in lab automation setups for sample handling, fluid transfer, or other instrument control tasks.

This is a multi-axis motion controller used to drive motorized stages, translation axes, or other laboratory mechanisms, while also providing digital and analog I/O for interlocks, triggering, and signal readback. It is commonly used for precise positioning, automated scanning, sample movement, and integrated instrument control.

A GenICam/GenTL-compatible machine vision camera or imaging device used in laboratories for image acquisition, machine vision, microscopy, and automated inspection. Such devices can typically be enumerated, connected, and used to stream 2D image data.

An industrial or machine-vision camera that transfers images through the GenICam/GenTL standard. It is used in laboratories for microscopy imaging, sample observation, process documentation, and automated visual inspection, supporting single-frame or continuous image acquisition.

This is an industrial digital camera that communicates and streams image data over Gigabit Ethernet. It can provide raw or color image data and is commonly used in laboratories for microscopy, machine vision, automated inspection, and other setups requiring stable image acquisition over longer cable distances.

A Gilson laboratory instrument that uses the GSIOC serial communication protocol, commonly found in devices for liquid handling, sample introduction, pumping, or collection. Such instruments are typically used in analytical chemistry and laboratory automation workflows for sample transfer, injection control, and fluid-path operations.

This is a software component that submits tasks to a distributed task queue over HTTP. It can generate and push per-frame processing tasks and is typically used in cluster workflows for microscopy images or other frame-based data.

A software component for submitting rules and frame-level tasks over HTTP to a laboratory data-processing cluster, commonly used in automated workflows for microscopy and other experimental data analysis.

Hamilton STAR automated liquid handling platform for laboratory aspiration, dispensing, tip handling, liquid level detection, plate and carrier transport, with control of iSWAP, the CoRe 96 head, autoload carrier handling, and some connected heating/cooling modules.

The Hamilton Vantage is an automated liquid handling workstation used for laboratory pipetting, tip pickup and ejection, liquid aspiration and dispensing, 96-channel plate processing, liquid level detection, and moving microplates or other labware with an integrated gripper.

A mechanical tilting module for laboratory automation platforms that tilts sample carriers to defined angles or positions to support liquid draining, settling, separation, or controlled sample handling. Depending on configuration, the module may also include heating, an encoder, sensor inputs, open-collector outputs, and a waste pump.

A benchtop recirculating chiller and temperature-control unit that circulates heat-transfer fluid to provide stable temperature control for a bath or external laboratory equipment. It is commonly used in labs to maintain a set temperature, monitor bath temperature, and change temperature using ramps or control programs.

A motorized motion axis used in laboratory and beamline systems to drive linear or rotary positioning mechanisms for precise adjustment of samples, optics, or diagnostics. This type of motor supports homing, limit management, status monitoring, and fault clearing, making it suitable for experiments that require reliable repeatable positioning.

A thermoelectric temperature control box for laboratory temperature-control modules. It provides control and device interaction for heating/cooling accessories, and is commonly used for managing sample, plate, or workflow temperatures.

This is a USB-connected ultrasound probe that performs standard ultrasound imaging and supports Doppler-related acquisition. It is used in laboratories or teaching environments for structural observation, flow-related measurements, and dynamic image recording. Depending on the probe design, the device may also include an internal motor for mechanical scanning.

The JULABO F32-HD is a laboratory recirculating chiller/thermostatic unit that provides stable temperature control to external instruments or experimental setups by circulating coolant. It is used in lab systems that require continuous heat removal and controlled operating temperature.

A temperature controller for laboratory temperature regulation and monitoring. It can read the current temperature, setpoint, heater output duty cycle, and heater on/off state, and supports task preparation, measurement, stopping, and reset operations.

Jubilee is a benchtop multi-axis motion platform for laboratory automation with automatic tool changing and deck-based workspace configuration. It can move precisely along axes such as X/Y/Z/U and work with pipetting, syringe, or other end tools for positioning, tool pickup and parking, labware placement, and sample-handling tasks in general lab automation workflows.

The Julabo FP50 is a laboratory recirculating chiller that provides stable cooling and temperature control to external equipment or experimental processes through circulating fluid. It is used where instruments, samples, or setups need a controlled operating temperature.

The Julabo Magio MS-1000F is a laboratory recirculating chiller and temperature control unit that circulates thermal fluid to provide stable cooling and heating for external equipment or experimental processes. It is commonly used for instrument cooling, jacketed reactor temperature control, sample environment conditioning, and other applications requiring precise circulating temperature management.

JULABO temperature circulation equipment is a family of benchtop liquid temperature control devices, including heating circulators, refrigerated/heating circulators, cryo-compact circulators, and recirculating coolers. They circulate a heat-transfer fluid to provide stable heating, cooling, or constant-temperature control for external equipment or samples, commonly used with reactors, condensers, analytical instruments, and other laboratory systems requiring precise temperature management.

records.name_en: Keithley 2400 / Lake Shore 350 Experiment Control Component
records.description_en: A non-physical software component that coordinates experiments involving a Keithley 2400 source meter and a Lake Shore 350 temperature controller. It handles instrument connection, configuration, temperature readback, heater-range and setpoint control, temperature ramping, electrical measurement readout, and GUI creation, styling, logging, and UI state management.
A scientific area detector camera used to acquire 2D images or spectroscopy-related signals, commonly used in laboratory optical measurements, low-light imaging, and spectroscopic experiments.
An axis-control module in Luminos positioning systems for precision motion on linear or rotational axes.
A pitch-axis control module in Luminos positioning systems for precise angular adjustment.
A roll-axis control module in Luminos positioning systems for precise angular adjustment.
